items.title: Stone Island Brings NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026
items.summary:
Stone Island took NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026, staging a dedicated installation at Capsule Plaza Shanghai @ IYOUTH from November 10 to 15. Designed with Milan studio NM3 , the space marked the installation's China debut following its first outing at Milan Design Week in April.

First launched by Massimo Osti between 1989 and 1994, NO SEASONS returns as a study in a single silhouette. One hooded jacket comes in six proprietary fabrics: Tela Resinata, Nylon Prismatico-TC, Raso Gommato, David-TC, Crinkle Reps NY and Panno. All six are dyed in lead-gray "piombo," so the material does the talking. Standouts include Tela Resinata, an evolution of the brand's foundational Tela Stella canvas, and David-TC, garment-dyed under pressure at up to 130°C for a compressed, textured hand.

NM3 carried that logic into the space. Four powder-coated steel benches, upholstered in the same six fabrics, anchored the room, while the jackets sat on black metal shelving raised to eye level on a new plinth. "NO SEASONS is all about material. And so is our work," NM3 co-founder Nicolò Ornaghi told Hypebeast. "We solve all the design problem[s] basically using one single detail. So it's a metal sheet that is bent and screwed. That's it."
Co-founder Francesco Zorzi saw the same approach in the collection. "It's actually the same attitude that Stone Island operated with in this collection," he said. "It's one jacket, one design, extremely well done, crazy good details, that works all season."

An LED wall screened the collection's new global campaign film by Capsule, while SYLOW, the new Stone…
items.t: Stone Island Brings NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026

Diagonal lines running off the strip inject a sense of motion, while exposed carbon fiber covers much of the car’s aero, including its towering active rear wing. To ensure the GTD 1901 lives up to its name, Ford’s aerodynamic performance Package comes standard, and buyers can opt for magnesium wheels in Black or Luster Nickel to shave over 50 pounds of unsprung weight.

Rolls-Royce Motor Cars has unveiled the Backgammon Set, a playable objet d’art built by the marque’s Bespoke Collective at the Home of Rolls-Royce at Goodwood. It sets one of the oldest known board games inside a mechanical case engineered with the same rigor as the marque’s cars, and it’s made to sit in a client’s home as a working game and a permanent display piece.

The set is built around a proprietary hinge machined from a single billet of aluminum, hand-polished, then anodized. As the case swings open, the central spine turns the opposite way to reveal the playing pieces and the board underneath. A Spirit of Ecstasy mounted on the hinge always turns upright, wherever the board comes to rest, using the same idea as the self-leveling wheel center caps on a Rolls-Royce . The counters are stored inside the spine. The precision dice, the doubling die and two dice shakers sit around a removable plinth that also works as the bar for captured counters.

Designed by long-time collaborator Vittorio Strosek, the aim was to enhance the original, rather than creating something entirely different from what Ferrari originally intended.

Constructed entirely from high-strength, lightweight carbon fiber, the N-Largo kit dramatically alters the 12Cilindri’s proportions, widening the front by 7 cm, and pushing out the rear by a substantial 13 cm. Refined in a wind tunnel, the new front fascia replaces the standard car’s Daytona-inspired black band in favor of a larger intake system, and an integrated spoiler engineered to reduce front-axle lift at high speeds. The most striking change they did is a custom one-piece carbon hood, which features an opening that prominently showcases the V12 engine’s dual red intake manifolds.

At the rear, Novitec eliminates the rear window entirely in favor of a carbon fiber lid with three narrow viewing slits to save weight. Globe-Trotter has unveiled GT897, a new collection that asks how light one of its cases could get. The name nods to 1897, the year the British luggage house was founded, and the line is its slimmest and lightest take on the signature case so far. Since then, every Globe-Trotter suitcase has been handmade in Hertfordshire, England, by artisans using original Victorian-era methods and machinery, and the brand’s cases have been carried by figures ranging from Captain Robert Falcon Scott and Queen Elizabeth II to Eddie Redmayne and Kate Moss. GT897 is built for frequent, spontaneous travel, whether that means long-haul flights, city breaks, business trips or last-minute weekends. It gives first-time buyers a new way into the brand and gives longtime owners a more relaxed alternative to the classic case.

The biggest change is the opening. The traditional frame and locks are gone, replaced by a zip-around construction that softens the case’s curves and trims its profile. The details that identify a Globe-Trotter are still there: Vulcanised Fibreboard, leather trims, nickel hardware and exposed rivets, so the case reads as Globe-Trotter from across a room and shows its new form up close.

items.title: Nike Is Reinventing Air for the Next 50 Years With Tuned Air
items.summary:
Summary 

Nike debuts Tuned Air, a digital printing process for custom cushioning.It removes rigid structures to create tailored, limitless underfoot sensations.The technology launches for runners in late 2027 before broader expansion.

Nike has introduced Tuned Air, a new way of making its Air cushioning units that the brand presents as the next chapter in nearly 50 years of Air innovation.

Instead of relying on traditional pins, rigid zones and the unit’s height to shape how Air behaves, Tuned Air uses a proprietary digital ink printed inside each unit, which Nike says took about a decade to develop. A selective lamination process then bonds the unit’s internal core only where no ink has been applied, letting Nike’s engineers control each unit’s internal structure with much greater precision.

The result opens up a far wider range of shapes, geometries and visual designs, giving Nike finer control over how Air looks, feels and performs. The name has precedent: “Tuned Air” was also the cushioning system behind the Air Max Plus, the 1998 runner better known as the TN, though Nike’s announcement presents the new technology on its own terms.

Following an exclusive sneak peek during Nike's World of Athletes showcase in this month, the innovative cushioning system is scheduled to make its official retail debut for runners in late 2027. This initial performance running launch will serve as the foundation for a much wider expansion, with the Tuned Air technology slated to be integrated across multiple athletic disciplines and the broader Nike Sportswear lineup. By removing…
items.t: Nike Is Reinventing Air for the Next 50 Years With Tuned Air

items.title: The Slim d’Hermès “Sous le charme d’Orphée” Brings the Myth of Orpheus to the Wrist
items.summary:
Summary 

Hermès adapts Alice Shirley’s Sous le charme d’Orphée scarf into a Slim d’Hermès dial.Engraving, miniature painting and pink opal cabochons depict a horse beneath a pomegranate tree.Only 12 white gold pieces will be made.

Hermès has unveiled an artistic addition to its minimalist dress watch family with the Slim d'Hermès Sous le charme d'Orphée limited edition. Drawing direct inspiration from the silk scarf of the same name designed by British artist Alice Shirley , the timepiece translates mythological storytelling onto a miniature nocturnal canvas.

Framed within the collection's signature slender 39.5mm white gold case, the dial depicts a horse galloping beneath a pomegranate tree under a shower of stars, which is a poetic nod to Orpheus, the legendary master of the lyre whose music enchanted the gods of the Underworld.
Bringing this fanciful scene to life requires an intricate convergence of traditional métiers d'art techniques executed across multiple stages. Set against a deep midnight blue enamel background, an engraver first sculpts the pomegranate tree across multiple levels to reveal the organic grain of the trunk and the delicate taper of its branches.

Several crafts come together on the dial. An engraver first carves the tree in layers, bringing out the grain of the trunk and the detail of each branch. A miniature painter then adds color one layer at a time, building up the leaves, the horse, the butterflies and the flowers. Finally, pink opal cabochons are set individually as the pomegranate fruits, adding depth and a soft shine to the scene. The…
items.t: The Slim d’Hermès “Sous le charme d’Orphée” Brings the Myth of Orpheus to the Wrist

items.title: Inside Denis Villeneuve’s Decision to Cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond
items.summary:
Summary 

Denis Villeneuve confirmed to ‘GQ’ that he chose Robert Pattinson as James Bond, in consultation with his producers and the studioHis list for the role starts with a believable killer and runs through charisma, sensuality, dark humor and physical strengthCasting took longer than fans expected because Villeneuve made the franchise wait until he wrapped ‘Dune: Part Three’

Denis Villeneuve has broken down exactly what he wanted when he cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond for the franchise’s 26th film. In his GQ Men of the Year interview , the director went through the role trait by trait, describing a 007 built less around gadgets and tailoring and more around menace, magnetism and nerve.

Villeneuve’s first requirement is that the audience has to buy Bond as someone capable of killing. “The first quality is that I need to believe that this man is a killer, because more than a spy, Bond is an assassin,” he told GQ . He also wants a visible rage behind the eyes, a quality he says only some actors have.

Presence comes next on his list, starting with a kind of panache that doesn’t apologize for itself. Villeneuve described a man who pulls the whole room toward him the moment he walks in, with charisma strong enough to carry a scene on its own. He also wants Bond to be openly sensual, someone people are drawn to and who visibly enjoys himself.

The rougher traits matter just as much to him. Villeneuve wants a Bond with a dark sense of humor, who seems to enjoy being in serious trouble and doesn’t mind getting his hands dirty. Physically, he called for someone strong…
items.t: Inside Denis Villeneuve’s Decision to Cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond

Co-creator Alexander Woo frames the season around whether the public has grown numb to the danger, and whether some people have started to welcome it.

The Game Awards has revealed its 2026 nominees, and Rockstar Games ’ Grand Theft Auto VI leads the field with eight nominations, including Game of the Year. This year’s nominees span 112 games, individuals and teams, chosen by a global jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets.

GTA VI shows up across nearly every craft category, with nods for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score & Music, Best Audio Design and Best Action/Adventure. Manni L. Perez adds a Best Performance nomination for her role in the game. For Game of the Year, it faces IO Interactive’s 007 First Light , Remedy and Annapurna’s Control Resonant , S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero , Capcom’s Resident Evil Requiem and Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time .

Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem are the closest challengers with six nominations each, and Phantom Blade Zero follows with five. Among publishers, Nintendo leads with 12 nominations across its catalog. Capcom is next with 11, then Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine each.

items.title: The 14 best men’s boots for winter, from chelseas and lace-ups to wellies
items.summary:
Whether you want minimalist or heritage, waterproof or suede, our menswear expert has rounded up the most stylish pairs for every occasion and outfit

• The best men’s coats for autumn and winter

I haven’t always worn boots. For years I wrote them off – at 5ft 8in, I was convinced anything above the ankle would make my legs look shorter. Then I started wearing them with the right trousers – a straight leg that falls over the top – and realised I’d spent a decade getting winter wrong. All anyone sees is a smart pair of shoes that happens to keep your ankles warm.

Here’s the thing: boots needn’t be intimidating. They’re just the wintry version of the leather shoes you already own. A chelsea is your loafer – it goes with pretty much everything in your wardrobe and every event in your diary, Christmas parties included. A derby boot is laced up, a bit sturdier and just as happy with jeans. The chukka is your weekend trainer. And the chunky, rubber-soled ones? Just think of them as an umbrella for your feet.
